arxiv-2204-06248.title: Distributed Coalgebraic Partition Refinement
arxiv-2204-06248.creator: Fabian Birkmann, Hans-Peter Deifel✉ ,, Stefan Milius
arxiv-2204-06248.description: Abstract Partition refinement is a method for minimizing automata and transition systems of various types. Recently, a new partition refinement algorithm and associated tool CoPaR were developed that are generic in the transition type of the input system and match the theoretical run time of the best known algorithms for many concrete system types.

arxiv-2309-09014.title: Electronic and Topological Properties of a Topological Insulator Thin Film Sandwiched between Ferromagnetic Insulators
arxiv-2309-09014.creator: P. Pigoń 1 , A. Dyrdał 2
arxiv-2309-09014.description: Abstract We consider a thin film of a topological insulator (TI) sandwiched between two ferromagnetic (FM) layers. The system is additionally under an external gate voltage. The surface electron states of TI are magnetized due to the magnetic proximity effect to the ferromagnetic layers.

arxiv-2312-14342.title: Identifying topologically associating domains using differential kernels
arxiv-2312-14342.creator: Luka Maisuradze
arxiv-2312-14342.description: Abstract Abstract Chromatin is a polymer complex of DNA and proteins that regulates gene expression. The three-dimensional (3D) structure and organization of chromatin controls DNA transcription and replication. High-throughput chromatin conformation capture techniques generate Hi-C maps that can provide insight into the 3D structure of chromatin.

arxiv-2504-07293.title: Small-Cell-Based Fast Active Learning of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
arxiv-2504-07293.creator: Zijian Meng, Hao Sun, Edmanuel Torres, Christopher Maxwell, Ryan Eric Grant, Laurent Karim Béland
arxiv-2504-07293.description: Abstract Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are often trained with on-the-fly active learning, where sampled configurations from atomistic simulations are added to the training set. However, this approach is limited by the high computational cost of ab initio calculations for large systems.

pmc-11375684.title: Mendelian randomization study of sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in cardiac and renal diseases
pmc-11375684.creator: Lei Chen, Yongdi Zuo, Manrong He, Lijin Duo, Wanxin Tang
pmc-11375684.description: ObjectiveSodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) target the reabsorption of sodium and glucose in the kidney proximal tubules to reduce blood sugar levels. However, clinical randomized controlled trials on SGLT2i have yielded inconsistent results, necessitating further research into their efficacy and safety for specific cardiac and renal diseases.Methods“Sodium in urine” was selected as a downstream biomarker of SGLT2i.

pmc-11436789.title: Subtracting the background by reducing cell-free DNA’s confounding effects on Mycobacterium tuberculosis quantitation and the sputum microbiome
pmc-11436789.creator: Charissa C Naidoo, Rouxjeane Venter, Francesc Codony, Gemma Agustí, Natasha Kitchin, Selisha Naidoo, Hilary Monaco, Hridesh Mishra, Yonghua Li, Jose C Clemente, Robin M Warren, Leopoldo N Segal, Grant Theron
pmc-11436789.description: DNA characterisation in people with tuberculosis (TB) is critical for diagnostic and microbiome evaluations. However, extracellular DNA, more frequent in people on chemotherapy, confounds results. We evaluated whether nucleic acid dyes [propidium monoazide (PMA), PEMAX] and DNaseI could reduce this.

pmc-11664142.title: Nano hydroxyapatite-silica with a core-shell structure for long-term management of dentin hypersensitivity
pmc-11664142.creator: Yifan Wang, Shangsi Chen, Minjun Zhang, Lili Chen, Chenchen Zhou, Shenglong Tan
pmc-11664142.description: SummaryTeeth undergo continuous demineralization and remineralization influenced by dietary acid and saliva. Excessive dietary acid attack disrupts this balance, exposing dentin tubules and causing dental hypersensitivity (DH). Due to low acid resistance, traditional anti-DH regents such as calcium phosphate minerals fail in long-term occlusion of dentin tubules, resulting in recurrent attacks of DH.

pmc-12646978.title: Prevalence, Age of Onset, Age at Diagnosis, and Family History of Hidradenitis Suppurativa in Pediatric Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12646978.creator: Grace Xiong, Mohamed Ali, Erfan Ghani Kakhki, Annie Xiong, Raed Alhusayen, David Croitoru, Cathryn Sibbald, Vincent Piguet, Ilya Mukovozov
pmc-12646978.description: IntroductionHidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by recurrent nodules and abscesses in intertriginous areas, ultimately resulting in scarring and formation of sinus tracts. HS significantly impacts quality of life and can also affect pediatric populations. We aimed to determine the prevalence, family history, age of onset, and age at diagnosis of HS in pediatric populations.

Its pathogenesis mainly involves neointimal hyperplasia and persistent inflammation. Although antiproliferative drugs used clinically can temporarily slow restenosis, their effects are limited by short action duration and lack of precise regulation. pmc-12822286.title: How do sports participation and sports settings influence the mental health of children and adolescents? A systematic review of qualitative studies
pmc-12822286.creator: Linda Ooms, Wikke van Stam, Vassilis Sevdalis, Marie Overbye, Beatrix Algurén, Sandra Heck, Aurélie Van Hoye
pmc-12822286.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPromoting mental health through sports participation may be a promising strategy to support the mental health of children and adolescents. This systematic review investigated the perceptions of children and adolescents and of stakeholders close to this target group (e.g., teammates, coaches, parents) on 1) how sports participation influences the mental health of children and adolescents; and 2) factors in sports settings influencing this relationship.MethodsA systematic review of qualitative studies was performed.

pmc-13288151.title: Aging and Western Diet Synergistically Impair Hepatic Thyroid Hormone Signaling to Promote Metabolic Dysfunction‐Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) in Mice
pmc-13288151.creator: Xinru Zhang, Madhulika Tripathi, Chun Ting Goh, Chee Seng Chan, Anita Boelen, Paul M. Yen, Brijesh Kumar Singh, Eveline Bruinstroop
pmc-13288151.description: Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is primarily driven by a Western‐style diet and exacerbated with aging, yet underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Given the essential role of thyroid hormone (TH) in MASLD progression, we hypothesized that impaired intrahepatic TH action during aging promotes MASLD progression and severity of MASH with fibrosis.

pmc-13492536.title: Machine learning and deep learning predictive models for prognosis in patients with atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13492536.creator: Xiaoyi Wang, Tristan John Bampton, Dhani Dharmaprani, Rajiv Mahajan, Lyle John Palmer
pmc-13492536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo summarise the performance of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) prognostic models for atrial fibrillation (AF), compare their relative performances with non-artificial intelligence (AI) methods, and to identify key research gaps.Methods and analysisWe searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and ProQuest from inception to 21 October 2024 for cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and randomised controlled studies that used ML or DL models to predict clinical outcomes in AF patients.

uslaw-usc-t7-s4613.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 77 (Honey Research, Promotion, And Consumer Information). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Issuance of amended order To implement the amendments made to this chapter by section 605 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (other than subsection (m) of that section), the Secretary shall issue an amended order under section.
